verdict.justification: A is preferable because its payroll reconciliation flags the variance supported by the visible April sources: the $236,500 regular accrual plus $20,500 special IT accrual totals $257,000, versus the trial balance liability of $141,033, producing A’s $115,967 difference. B instead reports “difference 177,467.00,” an unexplained $61,500 increase that would misdirect CFO review of a material exception. Both packages retain the requested TOC structure, identify the excluded CFO tabs, reference source filenames, and clearly flag missing AP support and the prepaid-insurance discrepancy. B offers a useful additional “Schedule-to-GL Tie-Out” tab and more explicit draft labeling, but those presentation advantages do not outweigh the payroll discrepancy. A also lists Loan I and Loan II separately in the TOC, making the included interest schedules easier to locate.

decisive_issues.issue: The payroll variance does not reconcile to the visible April accrual amounts and trial balance; it exceeds the supported difference by $61,500.
